title: Professional Certificate in Agentic AI Systems
summary: Design and deploy production multi-agent systems with orchestration, memory, tool protocols, evaluation, observability, deployment, and security.
capstone: Production multi-agent system with tool protocol integration, evaluation suite, tracing, guardrails, and deployment runbook.
format: 18 weeks, online; weekly mentored sessions plus a monthly live faculty masterclass

credential.rule: Every approved required course at C or better. Required-course list and final grading policy TBC.
credential.sourceDraftRules: Historical source additionally proposes 70% overall, all labs, capstone pass, and 80% participation/approved alternative. These are draft proposals, not activated issuance rules.

support: Scholarion AI Teaching Assistant (coaches; never completes graded work)
structure: Block B (Weeks 10–18): Production multi-agent systems; final exam replaced by capstone defense
weeks: 0 (optional)
Python and tooling refresher: VS Code, Colab, Git, virtual environments, API basics
Agentic systems: autonomy levels, agent loops, and when not to use agents
LLM foundations for builders: tokens, context, sampling, structured output, cost and latency
Instruction design for agents: system prompts and output schemas
Tool use and function calling: error handling and idempotent tools
Retrieval systems: embeddings, chunking, vector stores, hybrid search and reranking
Agentic RAG: routing, query planning, self-correction and citation grounding
Planning and reasoning patterns: reason-act loops, plan-and-execute and reflection
Memory and context management: short/long-term memory, summarization and context budgets
Midterm project plus Block A exam
Small language models for agents: local inference and SLM/LLM routing
Multi-agent architectures: orchestrator–worker, hierarchical, critic/reviewer and handoffs
Frameworks lab: graph-based orchestration and role-based crews; versions verified at build time
Tool and context protocols such as MCP: secure servers and clients
Agentic coding: repository tasks, test-first workflows and review gates
Evaluation: task success, trajectory evaluation, calibrated LLM-as-judge and regression suites
Observability, security and guardrails: tracing, injection defense, permissions, sandboxing and human oversight
Deployment: APIs, containers, cost controls, monitoring and rollback
Capstone defense and demo day

projects.name: Dual-Source Market Insight Agent
projects.description: Combines structured financial data and unstructured filings/news using synthetic or public-domain sources into a cited insight report.

projects.name: Autonomous Research Analyst Agent
projects.description: Multi-step research with planning, web/document tools, source grading, citations and confidence levels.

projects.name: Loan Underwriting Assistant
projects.description: A multi-agent recommendation package for a human underwriter using synthetic applicants; includes audit trail, fair-lending bias testing across protected attributes, adverse-action reason codes, and an explicit human-decision step. The system never issues final credit decisions.

prerequisites: Python functions, JSON and HTTP concepts
delivery: Self-paced draft modules with proposed weekend workshops, peer discussion and office hours; no cohort scheduled.
outcomes: O1: Map decision boundaries and evidence requirements for a multi-agent service desk.
O2: Construct and explain a bounded prototype for a multi-agent service desk.
O3: Evaluate ordinary, ambiguous and adversarial cases against a baseline.
O4: Demonstrate privacy minimization, human approval and recoverable failure.
O5: Defend a agent systems engineering portfolio with reproducible evidence and limitations.

capstonePackage.exemplar: A fictional approval queue retains missing scores, routes uncertainty to review and never executes updates. Its evidence pack records input versions, thresholds, subgroup counts, failed cases and a rollback owner. Adapt this scaffold to the program brief. This is not a finished capstone solution.
capstonePackage.peerReview: A peer challenges an unsupported claim and repeats one test; the author documents the response.
capstonePackage.status: Draft brief; finished program-specific exemplars require SME authoring.

evaluationPlan.pre: Explain a bounded workflow before instruction and attempt the first practice pool.
evaluationPlan.post: Use unseen synthetic cases and compare outcome-aligned rubric scores.
evaluationPlan.analytics: Local practice attempts and module checkpoints, not official grades.

transferPolicy: No automatic credit. Map outcomes and assessed evidence; an educator approves equivalence and prevents duplicate credit. Dependencies #1–#14 remain TBC.
